articles.title: Get help and submit a useful IT request
articles.summary: Choose chat or a ticket, describe the impact, and give IT the details needed to help.

content.text: This guide is for employees using FixxFlow. A clear request helps IT identify the affected service and decide what to investigate first.
From Home, choose Open a ticket for a problem or request. Choose Start a chat for a conversation. Chat replies may not be immediate; you can return to the conversation later.

Use a short title naming the affected service and symptom. In the description, include when it started, your location, the device or equipment tag, and the exact error. Explain whether you can keep working and whether coworkers are affected. Choose the closest category if one is available.

List the checks you already tried. After creating the ticket, add a relevant screenshot or file. Crop out unrelated customer details and private information. Never include passwords, authenticator codes, payment details, or reset links.
Open My tickets to find the request again. Add updates to the same ticket so the conversation stays together.
Your request appears in My tickets with a ticket number and status. If submission fails, keep your description and retry after checking your connection.

For an urgent outage or suspected security incident, also use your established workplace contact method. A ticket records the issue but does not guarantee an immediate response. If FixxFlow itself is inaccessible, contact IT outside the app.

articles.title: Follow a ticket, reply to IT, or reopen an issue
articles.summary: Find your request, understand its status, and keep the troubleshooting conversation in one place.

content.text: This guide covers the employee ticket view. Your organization’s IT team manages assignment and priority.
Choose My tickets, then select the relevant subject. Search using words from the title or the ticket number. Check the latest reply before sending another message.

New means the request has been recorded. Open or In progress means it is being handled. Waiting on user means IT needs information from you. On hold means work is paused. Resolved means a solution has been recorded; Closed means the request has been closed.

Use the reply field to answer IT’s questions. Describe what changed and whether the suggested fix helped. Add an attachment when it explains the problem, removing unrelated personal or customer information first.
If a resolved or closed request still has the same issue, use Reopen request. Explain what is still happening. For a different problem, create a new request instead.
Confirm your reply appears in the conversation or the reopened ticket shows its new status. Do not repeatedly resubmit while a request is sending.
If the ticket will not load or a reply fails, keep the unsent text and retry. If work is blocked, use your established IT contact method and include the ticket number.

articles.title: Reset your FixxFlow password
articles.summary: Recover access to FixxFlow and troubleshoot a missing or expired reset email.

content.text: These steps reset your FixxFlow password only. They do not change your email, device, or other workplace passwords.
1. Request a reset from the sign-in page
Open your usual FixxFlow sign-in page directly and choose Forgot password? Enter your work email and select Send reset link. Use the address associated with your existing account.
Check your inbox and junk folder. If you requested several emails, use the newest one. Treat the link as private: anyone with it may be able to act on your account.

Enter and confirm a unique password with at least eight characters, as required by FixxFlow. Prefer a longer passphrase or a password generated by your approved password manager. Save the change and sign in again.
If you enabled an authenticator, use its current six-digit code. Changing your password does not remove multi-factor authentication.
You can sign in with the new password and reach your workspace. An inactive or unassigned account may still need an administrator’s help.
If no email arrives, the link is rejected, or you cannot access your work inbox or authenticator, contact IT through an established alternative channel. Do not send your password or reset link.

articles.title: Set up an authenticator for FixxFlow
articles.summary: Add a second sign-in check and prepare a backup before changing phones.

content.text: FixxFlow supports six-digit codes from an authenticator app. Keep access to an existing verified authenticator while setting up another one.
Sign in to FixxFlow and choose Security in the account navigation. Under Multi-factor authentication, choose Add authenticator.
Use an authenticator approved for your workplace. Scan the displayed QR code, or enter the displayed setup secret into the app. Keep both private; do not attach them to a ticket.
Enter the six-digit code currently displayed in the authenticator, then select Verify and enable. If a code is about to expire, wait for the next one and try again.

Add and verify a second factor while you still have access to your current one. Confirm the replacement can generate accepted codes before removing an old factor. FixxFlow does not present downloadable recovery codes in this setup flow.
FixxFlow shows Authenticator enabled and lists a verified factor. At the next sign-in, complete the verification prompt with the current code.

If verification keeps failing, check that the phone uses automatic date and time. If you lost every verified authenticator, contact IT outside the app for help; do not create a duplicate organization to regain access.

articles.title: Troubleshoot Wi-Fi or an unavailable internet connection
articles.summary: Check whether a connection problem affects your device, one service, or other people.

content.text: Use these checks on your own work device. Network names and sign-in methods come from your IT team; do not guess them or change shared network equipment.
Confirm Wi-Fi is enabled and airplane mode is off. Select the workplace network IT has told you to use. If connected by cable, check that the cable is seated at your device or dock.

Try a second familiar work website. If only one service fails, note its name and exact error. Ask a nearby coworker whether they have the same problem without sharing passwords or using their account.

Save online work first. Disconnect and reconnect your device’s Wi-Fi once. Move to a location with a stronger signal if practical. On a shared business network, leave routers, access points, and network resets to IT.
Note your building or room, network name, time, signal strength, and whether you see connected but no internet. Do not bypass certificate warnings or install profiles from an unexpected sign-in page.
Open the affected work service again. A Wi-Fi connection indicator alone does not confirm that the service is reachable.
Contact IT if several people are affected, the expected network is missing, or reconnecting does not help. If you cannot reach FixxFlow, use your established alternative contact method.

articles.title: A work service or VPN will not connect
articles.summary: Separate internet, remote-access, and account problems before contacting IT.

content.text: This guide applies only if IT has provided remote access or a VPN. It does not assume your organization has a VPN or that every work service requires one.
Open a familiar public website. If it also fails, first troubleshoot the local connection. Record whether you are at work, at home, or using another network.
Open only the remote-access application supplied by IT and use the existing profile. Do not invent a server address, install a free VPN, or change security settings to make a connection work.
Note whether the connection times out, rejects your account, or asks for verification. Approve only sign-in attempts you initiated. Stop repeated password guesses if access is rejected.
If the connection succeeds but the service still fails, record the service name and the exact error. A connected VPN does not by itself grant access to every application.
The required service opens under your own account. If access remains denied, IT may need to check permissions or service availability.

Send IT the application name, error, approximate time, location, and whether ordinary websites work. Exclude passwords, codes, and connection secrets. Use another contact method if FixxFlow cannot be reached.

articles.title: Troubleshoot email that will not send or receive
articles.summary: Identify whether the issue affects one message, your mail app, or the mailbox itself.

content.text: These checks work across common workplace email tools. Use only your organization’s approved mail app and webmail address.
Confirm a familiar website opens, then verify you are looking at the correct work mailbox. Read any disconnected, storage, or sign-in message rather than repeatedly sending the same email.
For a sending problem, check the recipient address and look in Outbox or Drafts. If you receive a delivery failure, keep its error code. Do not delete unsent work while troubleshooting.
If IT provides webmail, open its known address directly. If mail works there but not in the app, save drafts and restart the app. Do not remove and recreate the account without IT’s guidance.
Determine whether all messages are affected or only one sender or recipient. Note the most recent message that worked. Avoid sending sensitive content to personal email as a workaround.
Confirm the message leaves Outbox and, when necessary, check receipt with the intended recipient through another channel. A sent message is not proof it was read.
Contact IT with the mail app, device, time, and delivery error. Report storage or account warnings. Do not permanently delete business records just to clear space without guidance.
Microsoft: Outlook sending and receiving problems

articles.title: Find a missing email or an expected reset message
articles.summary: Check the right mailbox and folders before asking for another copy.

content.text: Use this when you expect a message but cannot find it. For a suspicious message, use the phishing guide before interacting with its contents.
Check which work email address the sender used and which mailbox you have open. Shared mailboxes and personal work inboxes are different destinations.
Search by sender, a few subject words, or the date. Check Junk or Spam, Archive, and Deleted items. Clear active inbox filters that might be hiding older or unread messages.
Ask the sender through a known channel whether they received a delivery failure. Give them the correct work address, but do not request repeated copies of sensitive messages.
For FixxFlow password resets, request a fresh email from the known sign-in page if needed and use the latest link. Do not forward reset emails to someone else or use an unexpected link to sign in.
If you locate the message, confirm its sender and context before opening links or attachments. Keep business mail in your approved workplace mailbox.

If messages from one sender repeatedly disappear, give IT the sender address, expected recipient, subject without sensitive details, and approximate sending time. IT can investigate filtering and delivery.

articles.title: A printer is offline or your document will not print
articles.summary: Check the selected printer and your own print job without disrupting shared equipment.

content.text: This guide covers basic checks for a workplace printer. Follow posted equipment instructions and ask IT before restarting shared printers or changing their configuration.
In the print dialog, confirm you selected the intended workplace printer, not a PDF destination or another location. Note the printer name and its location or equipment tag.
Check for a clear message such as no paper, cover open, or low supplies. Refill only user-accessible supplies you are trained to handle. Do not force a paper jam or open service panels.
Look for a paused or failed job in your print queue. Cancel only your own duplicate or unwanted jobs if allowed. Do not clear a shared queue or change another person’s job.
Check whether one short document prints from an approved app. If other people cannot print either, report the shared problem rather than repeatedly sending jobs.
Collect the printed page promptly and check that all pages are yours. If the printer begins working later, watch for delayed duplicate jobs.
Contact IT with the printer name, exact display message, document type, and whether other users are affected. Avoid attaching confidential documents solely to demonstrate a printing failure.
Microsoft: Printer connection and printing problems

articles.title: An external monitor is blank or shows no signal
articles.summary: Check power, input selection, and the connection to your computer or dock.

content.text: These checks are for a monitor connected to your work computer. Stop if cables or equipment are damaged; arrange help instead of opening equipment.
Check its power light and use the monitor’s own menu if available. A menu that appears while the desktop does not can help distinguish the display from the computer connection.
Use the monitor controls to choose the input that matches the connected cable, such as HDMI or DisplayPort. Do not move another employee’s equipment to test.
Secure the video cable at the monitor and your computer or dock. If using a dock, confirm its power connection. Save work before disconnecting a dock that also carries network or storage connections.
Open your computer’s display settings and check whether an additional display is detected. If you know the supported display mode, choose it. Leave driver installation and hardware changes to IT.
The expected desktop appears and remains stable. If the display flickers or disconnects, record when it happens and which cable or dock is involved.
Provide IT with the monitor and computer models or equipment tags, the dock type, and the exact message on the display. Mention whether the built-in screen still works.

articles.title: A website will not load or the browser stops responding
articles.summary: Narrow down a website problem while protecting unsaved work and account access.

content.text: Use this for FixxFlow or another approved work website. If a page shows a certificate or security warning, stop and report it instead of bypassing it.
Copy unsent text into an approved work location if possible. Record the page address without private tokens and the exact error before refreshing.
Open a familiar work website. If every page fails, troubleshoot the connection. If only one service fails, note that distinction for IT.

Reload once. If the browser remains unresponsive, save other work and close unused tabs. Restart the browser when safe. Opening the same approved service in another IT-approved browser can help identify a browser-specific problem.

Do not disable managed extensions, download a repair utility from an advert, or clear every saved password to troubleshoot. Clearing site data may sign you out and discard local drafts; ask IT before taking that step.
The page loads and the original task works. After a failed submission, check whether the ticket or message already exists before submitting again.
Share the service name, browser, device, error, and time. Include whether other sites or coworkers are affected. Remove session tokens and personal information from screenshots.
Google Chrome Help: Browser crashes or will not open

articles.title: Request software or access to a work application
articles.summary: Give IT the business need and access details without sharing accounts or installing unapproved software.

content.text: Use this when you need a new application, a license, or permission to an existing service. Submitting a request does not itself approve a purchase or grant access.
Open the application from your usual approved launcher or bookmark and verify you are using your own work account. Record an access-denied message rather than trying a coworker’s credentials.
2. Describe the work you need to do

Create a ticket naming the application, the task, who needs access, and when it is needed. State whether you need to view information, edit it, or administer a service. Request only the access needed for your work.

Give the device type or equipment tag and any approval you have already obtained. If you do not know the approval process, say so and ask IT to route the request. Do not invent an approver or promise a purchase.
Use the installation or sign-in instructions IT supplies through a trusted channel. Do not install cracked software, share licenses, or enter workplace data into a personal trial account.
Confirm the approved task works under your own account. Tell IT if the application opens but the required feature is still unavailable.
Update the ticket if your deadline changes, an installer asks for administrator credentials, or you receive unexpected access. Never put license secrets or passwords into the request.

articles.title: Report a suspicious email, message, or sign-in request
articles.summary: Recognize suspicious requests and tell IT promptly, including if you already interacted.

content.text: Phishing can arrive through email, chat, text, or a phone call. An urgent tone, unexpected attachment, or request for a password or payment is a reason to pause, even when the sender name looks familiar.
Do not open the attachment, follow the link, reply with information, or approve an unexpected authentication prompt. Verify unusual requests through a contact method you already know.
Use your workplace’s established reporting method or contact IT in FixxFlow. Describe the sender, subject, time, and what was requested. Do not circulate a suspicious link to coworkers.
If you clicked, downloaded a file, entered information, or approved a prompt, tell IT immediately. Describe the action and affected account; do not include the actual password or verification code.

If credentials were entered, use the service’s known website from a trusted device to change them and contact IT. Do not rely on a password change alone after a suspected compromise. Let IT guide further account and device checks.
Confirm IT received your report. A message disappearing from your inbox does not establish that the risk is resolved.
Use an established urgent contact method for suspected account compromise or fraudulent payment. FixxFlow chat is not guaranteed to be monitored immediately.
NIST: Recognizing and responding to phishing

articles.title: Report a lost or stolen work device
articles.summary: Give IT the information needed to assess account access and protect workplace information.

content.text: Report a missing laptop, phone, tablet, or other work device promptly. Do not wait until you know whether it was misplaced or stolen.
Use a trusted device and your established workplace contact method. If you can access FixxFlow, open a ticket, but also use the urgent contact route available to you.
2. Describe the device and last known location
Provide its type, equipment tag or serial number if known, when and where you last had it, and a safe way to contact you. State whether it was unlocked and whether it held work information.

Tell IT if the device contains your authenticator, work email, or active application sessions. Do not paste passwords or recovery secrets into the report. If you cannot sign in, keep using the alternative contact channel.

Ask IT about approved locking, session revocation, or other protection steps. Do not erase a managed device or remove it from management on your own. If you find it, tell IT before reconnecting it or resuming work.
Keep the incident reference and confirm IT has a way to reach you. A device marked missing still needs IT’s assessment before the incident can be considered resolved.
If you believe the device was stolen, follow your workplace’s physical-security reporting process as well. Do not attempt to recover it from another person yourself.

articles.title: Join a Teams meeting and use meeting chat
articles.summary: Find the right invitation, join with your work account, and understand meeting-chat access.

content.text: For employees attending Microsoft Teams meetings where Teams is an approved work service. Invitations, guest access, and chat availability depend on the organizer’s settings.
Use the meeting link in your calendar invitation. Confirm the organizer and meeting before opening an unexpected link. If prompted, choose the approved Teams app or browser option.
Use your work account when required. Before joining, check your microphone, speaker, and camera choices. Join a few minutes early; a lobby means the organizer may need to admit you.

Select Chat in the meeting controls to read or send messages. Keep confidential information within the intended audience. Guest and anonymous participants may have limited chat access, including after leaving.
Confirm you can hear the meeting and that your message appears in the intended meeting chat.

Contact the organizer for lobby, invitation, or presenter permissions. Contact IT for repeated sign-in or joining failures; include the error, device, app or browser, and time. Never send meeting passcodes in a public ticket.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Fix microphone or speaker problems in Teams
articles.summary: Check mute controls and the selected audio devices before reconnecting.

content.text: For approved Teams meetings on a computer. A room system or managed headset may require IT assistance.
Check the Teams microphone control and any physical headset mute switch or raised microphone boom. Confirm your headset is connected, charged, and not being used by another device.

In Teams settings, open Devices and choose the intended speaker and microphone. During a meeting, open the audio settings from the microphone menu. Check device volume too. Avoid joining nearby devices with their speakers and microphones active because this can cause echo.

If the microphone is blocked, check the app or browser microphone permission when allowed by company policy. Reconnect an external headset. Save other work before restarting Teams. If available in desktop Teams, use the test-call option.
Ask another participant to confirm they hear you and confirm you hear them. A test call is not available in every Teams client.
If permissions are managed or audio still fails, give IT the headset model, client version, error, and whether the built-in microphone works. Do not install an unapproved audio driver.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Fix a camera that will not work in Teams
articles.summary: Check the camera selection, privacy shutter, and allowed permissions.

content.text: For computer cameras in approved Teams meetings. Managed privacy settings should be handled by IT.
Open the privacy shutter if fitted. Reconnect an external camera and check its cable. Close other applications that may be using the camera.
In Teams device settings or meeting video settings, choose your intended camera and inspect the preview. Turn the camera on in the meeting controls if you want to appear on video.

Check camera permission for Teams or the meeting website. On a Mac, camera access is under System Settings, Privacy & Security, Camera. Restart Teams after an allowed permission change. Do not bypass a managed restriction.
Confirm the preview shows the intended view and another participant can see you when video is enabled.
Contact IT if the camera is missing, permissions are locked, or the preview remains blank. Include the camera model and whether another approved app can use it.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Share a screen or window in a Teams meeting
articles.summary: Present the intended content while keeping unrelated information out of view.

content.text: For approved Teams meetings. Sharing may be restricted to presenters by the organizer.
Open the document or application you need. Close unrelated windows and sensitive notifications. Check who is in the meeting before showing customer or employee information.

Select Share in the meeting controls. Choose a single window when it is enough, or your screen when needed. A shared screen can expose other windows you open. Include computer audio only when needed and available.

Confirm participants see the intended content, then select Stop sharing before moving to unrelated work. If Share is unavailable, ask the organizer about your presenter role. Browser and Mac screen-recording permissions may also affect sharing; use approved settings.
Ask a participant to confirm the shared view is readable and that sharing stops when you finish.
Contact IT if an allowed presenter still cannot share. Include your client or browser, operating system, and permission error. Do not grant remote control to an unknown participant.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Save and recover work in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint
articles.summary: Understand AutoSave, preserve copies, and check recovery after a crash.

content.text: For approved Microsoft Office desktop apps. AutoSave availability depends on the app, license, file format, and storage location.
Save to the approved work location and check the filename. Use Save a Copy before experimenting with an existing document so changes do not replace the original.

Supported Microsoft 365 files in OneDrive or SharePoint Online can use AutoSave. A local file may not. Check the AutoSave state and save regularly when it is off. AutoRecover helps after a crash but is not a backup or a guarantee.

After an unexpected closure, reopen the app and review Document Recovery if offered. Open recovered versions and save the useful one under a clear name. For an approved cloud file, check version history before replacing work. Keep the existing and recovered copies until verified.
Reopen the saved file from its intended folder and check the latest changes are present.

Contact IT promptly if work is missing or the file will not open. Give the filename, storage location, app, and approximate last successful save. Do not delete recovery files or promise a recoverable version exists.
Microsoft: Save, back up, and recover
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Export a Word document to PDF
articles.summary: Keep the editable original and check the exported file before sharing.

content.text: For Microsoft Word desktop on Windows or Mac. Menu names vary between versions.
Confirm the audience, page layout, and any comments or tracked changes. Resolve or exclude review markup as appropriate; hiding text is not a reliable way to redact confidential information.

Keep the editable Word file. Use File, Save As or Save a Copy, then choose PDF as the file type. Select the intended folder and save. On Windows, export options may let you choose pages and whether markup is included.
Open the PDF independently. Check page breaks, tables, links, and any signatures. Ensure it contains only the intended pages and review markup before sending it through an approved channel.
Confirm the recipient can read the final PDF and the editable original is still available.
Contact IT if export fails or the output loses important content. Provide the Word version and error; share the source document only with authorized support staff.
Microsoft: Save or convert to PDF
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Troubleshoot Excel formulas and unexpected results
articles.summary: Distinguish displayed formulas, text cells, and calculation errors.

content.text: For approved Excel workbooks. Financial, operational, and shared calculations should be reviewed with the workbook owner before changing their logic.

If many cells show formulas instead of results, check Formulas, Show Formulas. If only one cell shows formula text, check whether it is formatted as Text or has a leading apostrophe. Preserve a copy before making corrections.

Formulas normally begin with an equals sign. Inspect referenced cells and the exact error. A missing reference, invalid input, or division by zero requires fixing its cause; replacing every error with zero can hide a real problem.
3. Check calculation settings with the owner

If results seem stale, review calculation settings. A workbook may deliberately use manual calculation. Ask the owner before switching to automatic calculation or changing formulas in a shared workbook. For a text-formatted formula, correcting the format may also require re-entering the formula.
Compare a small, known example with the expected result and have the workbook owner review important calculations.
Contact IT for app failures or access problems; contact the workbook owner for formula logic. Include the error, cell reference, and Excel version without exposing unrelated confidential data.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Create and update an Outlook meeting invitation
articles.summary: Invite attendees, check the time zone, and send changes to participants.

content.text: For Outlook with an approved work account. Teams meeting options and availability information depend on account support and organization configuration.

In new Outlook, create a New event and invite attendees. In classic Outlook, use New Meeting. A personal appointment without attendees does not invite coworkers. Add a useful subject, date, start and end times, and location.

Confirm the calendar time zone, especially for participants in other countries. Use Scheduling Assistant when available, but external availability may be unknown. If your account supports it, enable the Teams meeting option for an online meeting. Review attendees and details before selecting Send.
3. Send updates from the original meeting

As organizer, open the original meeting to change its details, then send the update when prompted. Cancel through the meeting so attendees receive the cancellation; simply deleting your own view may not inform them.
Confirm the meeting appears in your calendar with the intended attendees and online details. Ask an attendee to confirm receipt if delivery is in doubt.
Contact IT if invitations fail, an expected Teams option is unavailable, or calendar times remain inconsistent. Provide the Outlook client and error; avoid posting private invitation links.
Microsoft: Schedule a meeting or event
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Troubleshoot a file that will not sync with OneDrive
articles.summary: Check the account, sync status, and space before changing files.

content.text: For an approved work OneDrive account. A file on your computer is not necessarily uploaded to the cloud.
Save open files. Note which copy contains the latest changes before renaming, moving, or replacing anything. Check the OneDrive icon and its status or error message.

Confirm internet access and the intended work account. If syncing is paused, resume it when appropriate. Check for a storage-full warning or an item requiring attention. Follow the specific displayed error instead of deleting files to force a sync.

Open OneDrive on the web using your work account and inspect the expected folder. Compare names and modification times. Keep unsynced work until you confirm it is safely uploaded. Do not unlink the account, reset OneDrive, or reinstall it on a managed device without IT guidance.
Confirm OneDrive reports the item is synced and the web copy contains the expected latest changes.
Contact IT if sync errors persist or the copies disagree. Include the status message, affected filename, account type, and time. Do not send passwords or private share links.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Find or restore a deleted cloud file
articles.summary: Check the correct account, recycle bin, and file owner without deleting other copies.

content.text: For approved OneDrive or Google Drive storage. Recovery depends on ownership, retention policies, and how the file was deleted.
Check the account, search the filename, and inspect the original folder. A shared file may have been moved or your access may have changed. Ask its owner before creating a replacement.

For OneDrive, open the web recycle bin and restore the intended item if available. For Google Drive, open Trash, select the file, and choose Restore. An online-only file may not be in the computer’s recycle bin.

Open the restored file and check its contents and location. Keep other copies until you know which is current. Do not empty the bin or permanently delete items while recovery is being investigated. Retention windows vary, so report missing important work promptly.
Confirm the correct version opens and intended colleagues still have appropriate access.

Contact IT immediately if the file is not in the bin, belongs to another person, or contains critical work. Include its name, owner, service, and approximate deletion time. Recovery is not guaranteed.
Microsoft: Delete and restore OneDrive files
Google: Recover a deleted Drive file
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Share a work file with the right people
articles.summary: Use named recipients and the minimum access needed for approved cloud storage.

content.text: For approved OneDrive, SharePoint, or Google Drive files. Company rules determine what may be shared externally.
Check whether the document contains customer, employee, or other restricted information. Verify recipients and external-sharing approval before granting access.

In Microsoft sharing settings, use Specific people when available. In Google Drive, keep General access Restricted and add the intended people. Give viewing access when editing is unnecessary. A folder or shared drive may confer inherited access that an individual-file setting does not remove.

Check the sharing or Manage access view after sending. Ask the intended recipient to confirm access. Review permissions when work ends and remove access you are authorized to remove. Avoid Anyone links for sensitive work.
Confirm the intended recipient can access the file at the correct permission level. Check the actual permission list rather than assuming a copied link is private.

Contact IT if external sharing is blocked, inherited permissions are unclear, or a file was exposed accidentally. Report the file and unintended audience promptly; never share login details as a workaround.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Check a Windows computer that is running slowly
articles.summary: Save work, check storage, and describe the slowdown before making major changes.

content.text: For Windows work computers. Managed maintenance and software removal should remain with IT.
1. Save work and narrow the problem
Note whether one app or the whole computer is slow, when it began, and whether colleagues are affected. Save documents, close unused apps, and restart at a suitable time.

Open Settings, System, Storage to inspect available space. Review cleanup recommendations carefully. Do not select Downloads or other folders without checking their contents, and do not delete system files or shared work. Ask IT if you are unsure what can be removed.

Try the same task again. Note unusually high fan activity, overheating, repeated crashes, or a nearly full drive. Avoid registry cleaners, unapproved optimization tools, and disabling security software.
Confirm the same task completes more reliably; record how long it takes if the slowdown continues.
Contact IT for repeated freezes, overheating, storage warnings, or a sudden unexplained slowdown. Include the device tag, affected apps, and steps tried.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Install approved updates on a work computer
articles.summary: Plan for restarts and follow managed Windows or Mac update settings.

content.text: For work Windows 11 or Mac devices. Company-managed update schedules take priority over general vendor guidance.
Save open work, connect power, and choose a time that will not interrupt a meeting or critical task. Confirm important work is stored in the approved backed-up location.

On Windows 11, open Settings, Windows Update. On a Mac, open System Settings, General, Software Update. Review the available update and any company instructions. Let IT handle locked settings or administrator prompts you are not authorized to approve.

Follow the approved update process and any required restart. Do not interrupt an installation by forcing power off. Major operating-system upgrades, beta releases, and unapproved drivers should be discussed with IT first.
After restarting, confirm you can sign in and use your key work apps. Check whether a further restart is required.
Contact IT for repeated update errors, a prolonged installation without progress, or broken work apps afterward. Include the device, update name or error, and time; do not bypass managed controls.
Source guidance reviewed October 6, 2026. App labels and available features can vary by version, license, and organization policy.

articles.title: Troubleshoot a mouse or keyboard that stops responding
articles.summary: Check power, cables, and the intended wireless connection.

content.text: For approved USB or Bluetooth input devices, especially on Windows work computers.
Check the cable, power switch, and batteries or charge. Reconnect a USB device or its receiver to an available port. If using a dock, check the dock’s power and connection too.

Keep a Bluetooth device close to the computer and confirm it is connected to the intended device. Some accessories switch between computers. Review Bluetooth settings if allowed; avoid removing a working pairing without a way to complete setup again.
If available, try another approved input device or port. Save work before restarting. Do not download drivers from an unknown site or change managed settings to force the device to work.
Confirm typing or pointer movement works consistently in an ordinary app.
Contact IT if the device remains unresponsive, pairing is blocked, or several USB accessories fail together. Include device models, connection type, and whether another port or approved device works.

articles.title: Respond to a fake technical-support warning
articles.summary: Recognize unsolicited repair demands and report any interaction promptly.

content.text: For unexpected calls, emails, or browser warnings claiming your work device needs urgent repair.
A scary warning does not establish that the device is infected. Do not call a number displayed in a suspicious pop-up, pay for a repair, or install a remote-access tool at a stranger’s request.

Do not enter credentials or security codes into the warning. Close the suspicious page if possible without interacting with its buttons. Contact your known IT team through FixxFlow or another established company channel.

Tell IT promptly if you entered information, paid, downloaded software, or granted remote access. Record the approximate time and what happened. Preserve useful evidence without reopening malicious links. Follow IT’s instructions for the affected device and accounts.
Confirm the warning is no longer being interacted with and IT has the details needed to assess any exposure.

Contact IT immediately after credentials, payment information, or remote control were shared. Do not conceal the interaction or attempt to erase evidence. IT can coordinate recovery based on what happened.

articles.title: Find official help articles and service-status information
articles.summary: Start with trusted support libraries and use status pages as one troubleshooting clue.

content.text: For employees looking for general guidance about approved Microsoft, Google, or Apple products. Public advice does not override company policy.

Use Microsoft Support for Teams, Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneDrive, and Windows. Google Workspace Learning Center covers approved Google work tools. Apple Support covers Mac and Apple devices. Search with the product name and exact error; match the app version where possible.

Google Workspace Status Dashboard reports supported Google service incidents. Microsoft’s public status page covers selected services; an organization’s Microsoft 365 business health may require its administrator to check the admin center. A clear public page does not prove your account or network is healthy.

Record the official article or incident link, affected service, time, and steps tried. Do not install repair tools from advertisements or assume every internet workaround is approved. Ask IT before changing managed configuration.
Confirm the article applies to your product and account type. Compare its result with what you actually see.
Contact IT if a guide does not fit, access is blocked, or your work remains affected. Include the error and relevant official link; IT can check tenant-specific health and permissions.
